title: Biosecurity Protocols
description: Standard operating procedure for preventing disease introduction and spread in aquaculture facilities. Covers visitor protocols, quarantine procedures for new stock, disinfection protocols, and disease outbreak response. Rigorous biosecurity protects organism health and facility viability.

steps.title: Biosecurity is Critical
steps.description: Disease introduction can devastate an entire facility within days. Once pathogens are introduced, they are extremely difficult to eliminate. Every person entering the facility is a potential vector. Strict adherence to biosecurity protocols protects all organisms, staff investments, and facility operations.
checklistItems: Understand that biosecurity failures can be catastrophic
Commit to following all protocols without exception
When in doubt, ask before acting

steps.title: Facility Access Control
steps.description: Access to aquaculture facilities must be controlled and limited to essential personnel. All visitors must be logged, briefed on protocols, and escorted. Establish secure perimeters with limited entry points. Post biosecurity signage at all entrances.

steps.title: Staff Entry Protocol
steps.description: All staff must follow entry protocol each time they enter the facility.
checklistItems: Sign entry log with name, date, and time
Confirm no contact with other aquaculture facilities in past 48 hours
If recent facility contact, report to supervisor before entry
Remove street shoes and don facility footwear
Step through footbath (verify disinfectant is fresh)
Wash hands thoroughly with antimicrobial soap
Don clean facility clothing if required
Proceed directly to assigned work area

steps.title: Visitor Management Protocol
steps.description: Visitors pose elevated biosecurity risk and require additional precautions.
checklistItems: Visitor appointment scheduled and approved in advance
Verify no recent contact with diseased animals
Issue disposable boot covers or facility footwear
Provide disposable coveralls if visiting production areas
Restrict visitor to approved areas only
Dispose of visitor PPE after use

steps.title: Footbath Management
steps.description: Footbaths are a primary barrier against pathogen introduction via footwear. Maintain footbaths at all entry points with fresh disinfectant. Replace disinfectant solution daily or more frequently if heavily used or visibly contaminated. Common disinfectants include quaternary ammonium compounds and iodophors.
checklistItems: Date and time of last change logged

steps.title: Hand Hygiene
steps.description: Hands are a major vector for pathogen transmission between systems. Wash hands with antimicrobial soap before and after handling organisms, between systems, and after handling potentially contaminated materials. Hand sanitizer is acceptable for interim use but not a replacement for washing.
checklistItems: Scrub all surfaces for at least 20 seconds
Use towel to turn off faucet

steps.title: Equipment Sharing Prohibitions
steps.description: Never share equipment between systems without proper disinfection. Dedicated equipment for each system is preferred. If equipment must be shared, thorough cleaning and disinfection is mandatory. Nets, siphons, buckets, and tools are common pathogen vectors.
checklistItems: Never move equipment between systems without disinfection
Maintain separate equipment for quarantine areas
Color-code equipment by system or area

steps.title: Equipment Disinfection Procedure
steps.description: When equipment must be moved between systems, follow complete disinfection protocol. Remove organic matter first (disinfectants are inactivated by organic debris). Soak or spray with appropriate disinfectant for required contact time. Rinse with clean water before use. Allow to dry if possible.
checklistItems: Maintain contact time per product label

steps.title: Common Disinfectants and Uses
steps.description: Different disinfectants are effective against different pathogens. Quaternary ammonium: Broad spectrum, safe for most surfaces. Iodophors: Effective against bacteria and viruses, can stain. Chlorine compounds: Highly effective, corrosive, must rinse well. Hydrogen peroxide: Environmentally friendly, short contact time. Always follow manufacturer dilution and contact time recommendations.

steps.title: Quarantine Procedures for New Stock
steps.description: All new organisms must be quarantined before introduction to main systems. Quarantine duration depends on species and disease risk but typically 2-4 weeks minimum. Quarantine systems should be physically isolated with separate equipment, water supply, and drainage.

steps.title: Receiving New Stock
steps.description: Follow receiving protocol for all incoming organisms.
checklistItems: Inspect shipping containers for leaks or damage
Note water temperature and conditions in shipping water
Acclimate organisms to quarantine system conditions
Place in designated quarantine system only
Label quarantine system with arrival date and source
Do not enter main production areas after handling new stock without complete decontamination

steps.title: Quarantine Monitoring
steps.description: Monitor quarantined organisms closely for signs of disease during the quarantine period.
checklistItems: Daily observation of behavior and appearance
Monitor for lethargy, loss of appetite, or abnormal swimming
Check for external lesions, discoloration, or parasites
Report any concerns to supervisor immediately

steps.title: Release from Quarantine
steps.description: Only release organisms from quarantine after completing full observation period with no disease signs. Supervisor must approve release. If any disease is suspected during quarantine, extend observation period and consider diagnostic testing before release.
checklistItems: Quarantine system can be cleaned and reset

steps.title: Daily Observation for Disease Signs
steps.description: Regular observation is the first line of disease detection. Train yourself to recognize normal behavior and appearance for each species. Any deviation may indicate early disease. Common warning signs include reduced feeding, lethargy, abnormal swimming, lesions, color changes, and increased mortality.

steps.title: Disease Outbreak Response
steps.description: If disease is suspected, act immediately to contain spread. Isolate affected system. Stop all movement of organisms, water, and equipment. Notify supervisor and initiate disease investigation. Do not panic but act decisively.
checklistItems: Stop all organism and water movement immediately

steps.title: Disease Sample Collection
steps.description: Proper sample collection is essential for accurate diagnosis. Collect moribund (dying but not dead) organisms when possible. Keep samples cool but not frozen unless instructed. Use sterile containers. Document sample source, date, and observations. Coordinate with diagnostic laboratory for specific requirements.
checklistItems: Keep samples cool (4C) unless otherwise directed
Label samples with date, system, species

steps.title: Mortality Management
steps.description: Remove dead organisms promptly to prevent disease spread and water quality degradation. Count and record all mortalities. Examine dead specimens for disease signs before disposal. Dispose of mortalities according to facility protocol. Never dispose of mortalities in a way that could contaminate water sources.
checklistItems: Refrigerate specimens for potential diagnosis if unusual
Never dispose in drains or water bodies

steps.title: End of Shift Biosecurity Checkout
steps.description: Complete biosecurity checklist before leaving facility.
checklistItems: All equipment returned to proper locations
Footbaths checked and refreshed if needed
